64: fn parse_name_value_opt<'a>(opts: &mut Options<'a>, opt: &'a OsStr) -> UResult<bool> {
65:     // is it a NAME=VALUE like opt ?
66:     let wrap = NativeStr::<'a>::new(opt);
67:     let split_o = wrap.split_once(&'=');
68:     if let Some((name, value)) = split_o {
69:         // yes, so push name, value pair
70:         opts.sets.push((name, value));
71:         Ok(false)
72:     } else {
73:         // no, it's a program-like opt
74:         parse_program_opt(opts, opt).map(|_| true)
75:     }
76: }

91:     // NOTE: config files are parsed using an INI parser b/c it's available and compatible with ".env"-style files
92:     //   ... * but support for actual INI files, although working, is not intended, nor claimed
93:     for &file in &opts.files {
94:         let conf = if file == "-" {
95:             let stdin = io::stdin();
96:             let mut stdin_locked = stdin.lock();
97:             Ini::read_from(&mut stdin_locked)

103:             conf.map_err(|e| USimpleError::new(1, format!("{}: {}", file.maybe_quote(), e)))?;

107:             for (key, value) in prop {
108:                 env::set_var(key, value);
109:             }
110:         }

415:     fn run_program(
416:         &mut self,
417:         opts: &Options<'_>,
418:         do_debug_printing: bool,
419:     ) -> Result<(), Box<dyn UError>> {
420:         let prog = Cow::from(opts.program[0]);
421:         #[cfg(unix)]
422:         let mut arg0 = prog.clone();
423:         #[cfg(not(unix))]
424:         let arg0 = prog.clone();
425:         let args = &opts.program[1..];
426: 
427:         /*
428:          * On Unix-like systems Command::status either ends up calling either fork or posix_spawnp
429:          * (which ends up calling clone). Keep using the current process would be ideal, but the
430:          * standard library contains many checks and fail-safes to ensure the process ends up being
431:          * created. This is much simpler than dealing with the hassles of calling execvp directly.
432:          */
433:         let mut cmd = process::Command::new(&*prog);
434:         cmd.args(args);
435: 
436:         if let Some(_argv0) = opts.argv0 {
437:             #[cfg(unix)]
438:             {
439:                 cmd.arg0(_argv0);
440:                 arg0 = Cow::Borrowed(_argv0);
441:                 if do_debug_printing {
442:                     eprintln!("argv0:     {}", arg0.quote());
443:                 }
444:             }
445: 
446:             #[cfg(not(unix))]
447:             return Err(USimpleError::new(
448:                 2,
449:                 "--argv0 is currently not supported on this platform",
450:             ));
451:         }
452: 
453:         if do_debug_printing {
454:             eprintln!("executing: {}", prog.maybe_quote());
455:             let arg_prefix = "   arg";
456:             eprintln!("{}[{}]= {}", arg_prefix, 0, arg0.quote());
457:             for (i, arg) in args.iter().enumerate() {
458:                 eprintln!("{}[{}]= {}", arg_prefix, i + 1, arg.quote());
459:             }
460:         }
461: 
462:         match cmd.status() {
463:             Ok(exit) if !exit.success() => {
464:                 #[cfg(unix)]
465:                 if let Some(exit_code) = exit.code() {
466:                     return Err(exit_code.into());
467:                 } else {
468:                     // `exit.code()` returns `None` on Unix when the process is terminated by a signal.
469:                     // See std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt for more information. This prints out
470:                     // the interrupted process and the signal it received.
471:                     let signal_code = exit.signal().unwrap();
472:                     let signal = Signal::try_from(signal_code).unwrap();
473: 
474:                     // We have to disable any handler that's installed by default.
475:                     // This ensures that we exit on this signal.
476:                     // For example, `SIGSEGV` and `SIGBUS` have default handlers installed in Rust.
477:                     // We ignore the errors because there is not much we can do if that fails anyway.
478:                     // SAFETY: The function is unsafe because installing functions is unsafe, but we are
479:                     // just defaulting to default behavior and not installing a function. Hence, the call
480:                     // is safe.
481:                     let _ = unsafe {
482:                         sigaction(
483:                             signal,
484:                             &SigAction::new(SigHandler::SigDfl, SaFlags::empty(), SigSet::all()),
485:                         )
486:                     };
487: 
488:                     let _ = raise(signal);
489:                 }
490:                 return Err(exit.code().unwrap().into());
491:             }
492:             Err(ref err)
493:                 if (err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound)
494:                     || (err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput) =>
495:             {
496:                 return Err(self.make_error_no_such_file_or_dir(prog.deref()));
497:             }
498:             Err(e) => {
499:                 uucore::show_error!("unknown error: {:?}", e);
500:                 return Err(126.into());
501:             }
502:             Ok(_) => (),
503:         }
504:         Ok(())
505:     }
506: }

519:     };
520:     let argv0 = matches.get_one::<OsString>("argv0").map(|s| s.as_os_str());

522:     let mut opts = Options {
523:         ignore_env,
524:         line_ending,
525:         running_directory,
526:         files,
527:         unsets,
528:         sets: vec![],
529:         program: vec![],

533:     let mut begin_prog_opts = false;

557: fn apply_specified_env_vars(opts: &Options<'_>) {
558:     // set specified env vars
559:     for (name, val) in &opts.sets {
560:         /*
561:          * set_var panics if name is an empty string
562:          * set_var internally calls setenv (on unix at least), while GNU env calls putenv instead.
563:          *
564:          * putenv returns successfully if provided with something like "=a" and modifies the environ
565:          * variable to contain "=a" inside it, effectively modifying the process' current environment
566:          * to contain a malformed string in it. Using GNU's implementation, the command `env =a`
567:          * prints out the malformed string and even invokes the child process with that environment.
568:          * This can be seen by using `env -i =a env` or `env -i =a cat /proc/self/environ`
569:          *
570:          * POSIX.1-2017 doesn't seem to mention what to do if the string is malformed (at least
571:          * not in "Chapter 8, Environment Variables" or in the definition for environ and various
572:          * exec*'s or in the description of env in the "Shell & Utilities" volume).
573:          *
574:          * It also doesn't specify any checks for putenv before modifying the environ variable, which
575:          * is likely why glibc doesn't do so. However, the first set_var argument cannot point to
576:          * an empty string or a string containing '='.
577:          *
578:          * There is no benefit in replicating GNU's env behavior, since it will only modify the
579:          * environment in weird ways
